story.

Keep fixed all background facts that are causally upstream of the intervention,
along with any other story details it does not affect. Update the intervened event
and every downstream consequence it changes so that the edited story remains causally
consistent with the original context.

Identify which statements in the story are causally affected by
the requested change. These are not to be treated as background facts,
even when explicitly stated. Update them where necessary; preserve only causally
unaffected details.

Before editing, silently generate relevant unstated facts implied by the story and actively
recall any ordinary world knowledge needed to determine the consequences. Use those facts
when updating the story.

Treat every requested change as externally fixed. Identify which events/facts in the story

Return only the fully edited story.

story: It was Alice's birthday and she had organized dinner with friends at a nice restaurant. After she finished work that day, she walked alone outside in the open for 30 minutes to get to the restaurant. She was a bit tired, but her spirits were immediately lifted when her friends complimented her hair and told her how lovely it looked. As they were leaving the restaurant after dinner, she lent her friend the umbrella that she had carried from work. She decided to take a taxi home because it had been raining heavily all day and the streets were wet.

With heavy rain and no cover also fixed, getting wet is the ordinary downstream consequence. The later loan must also disappear because the same absent umbrella cannot be lent. The compliment and taxi are preserved because neither is logically incompatible with wet hair or the missing umbrella.
